findings.evidence: I graduated from New Haven in 1915, and a little later I participated in that delayed Teutonic migration known as the Great War… so I decided to go East and learn the bond business… in the spring of twenty-two.
My house was at the very tip of the egg… It was Gatsby's mansion… Daisy was my second cousin once removed… to have dinner with the Tom Buchanans… in East Egg.
I first met Tom Buchanan's mistress… George B. Wilson. Cars bought and sold… the valley of ashes… Wilson? He thinks she goes to see her sister in New York.

There was music from my neighbour's house through the summer nights… By seven o'clock the orchestra has arrived… The party has begun… Gatsby, standing alone on the marble steps and looking from one group to another with approving eyes. He was not drinking.

I believe that on the first night I went to Gatsby's I was one of the few guests who had actually been invited… 'I'm Gatsby'… Meyer Wolfshiem? No, he's a gambler… He's the man who fixed the World's Series back in 1919.
One October day in nineteen-seventeen—said Jordan Baker… His name was Jay Gatsby… 'Gatsby bought that house so that Daisy would be just across the bay.'

'He wants to know if you'll invite Daisy to your house some afternoon, and then let him come over.'… Daisy's car turned into my lane… When I returned the rain had thinned. They were at either end of the couch… there was a change in Gatsby that was simply confounding. He literally glowed.

James Gatz—that was really, or at least legally, his name… his parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people… the beginning of his career—when he saw Dan Cody's yacht… he was in the drug business and then he was in the oil business.
findings.note: The abridgment covers James Gatz origins and Dan Cody tutelage; illicit enterprises referenced via bootlegging/drugstore accusations and Wolfshiem connection.

findings.evidence: Tom was evidently perturbed at Daisy's running around alone, for on the following Saturday night he came with her to Gatsby's party… she was appalled by West Egg… appalled by its raw vigour.
We all took the less explicable step of engaging the parlour of a suite in the Plaza Hotel… Tom: exposing Gatsby's drugstore/bootlegging dealings… 'I did love him once—but I loved you too.'
'Was Daisy driving?' 'Yes,' he said after a moment, 'but of course I'll say I was.'… Myrtle Wilson rushed out; the 'death car'… did not stop.

By half-past two he was in West Egg, asking the way to Gatsby's house… the chauffeur heard the shots… the laden mattress moved irregularly down the pool… the gardener saw Wilson's body a little way off in the grass.

She and Tom had gone away early that afternoon, and taken baggage with them… 'Left no address?'… It was Gatsby's father… About five o'clock our procession of three cars reached the cemetery… a handful of servants, all wet to the skin.
I saw Jordan Baker and talked over and around what had happened… I couldn't forgive him or like him… I decided to come back home.
Gatsby believed in the green light, the orgiastic future that year by year recedes before us… So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
